rv.q: Its 2019 debut, Ane City, was a one-woman jukebox journey through the Scottish city at night. New show Pushin’ Thirty – made with Glasgow’s A Play, A Pie and A Pint – is a two-hander that deals with similar themes of ambition, escape and ageing, and is similarly steeped in a deep affection for Dundee.
Pushin’ Thirty offers a fresh breath through a nostalgic heart of folk-styled music with an authentic tale which rejects melodrama for something easy to bite into.
If it all ends up being rather inconsequential, it nevertheless has considerable charm.

cn.t: Critics praise "Pushin Thirty" as a delicate and evocative exploration of friendship, with its gentle storytelling and relatable themes resonating positively in this Play, Pie and a Pint production.
